title: "AI Use"

## Proposed AI Usage
Prompt: using this data(https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/martinellis/nhl-game-data/data?select=game_teams_stats.csv) we want to use goals scored as a nominal response factor, fit a model after making the necessary adjustments for the model.

AI Response: 
Install required packages if you don't have them:
install.packages(c("tidyverse", "nnet", "caret"))

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(nnet)
library(caret)
```


1. Load Data

```{r}
df <- read_csv('game_teams_stats.csv')
```

2. Make Necessary Adjustments for Nominal Response Target
Bin goals into nominal categories: 'Low' (0-1), 'Medium' (2-3), 'High' (4+)

```{r}
df <- df %>%
mutate(
goals_nominal = case_when(
goals <= 1 ~ "Low_Goals",
goals <= 3 ~ "Medium_Goals",
TRUE ~ "High_Goals"
),
goals_nominal = as.factor(goals_nominal)
)
```

3. Feature Selection & Data Cleaning
Drop target leakage ('won', 'powerPlayGoals'), raw 'goals', and IDs

```{r}
leakage_cols <- c("goals", "won", "powerPlayGoals", "game_id", "team_id", "head_coach")
df_model <- df %>%
select(-any_of(leakage_cols)) %>%
mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
drop_na()
```

4. Train/Test Split (Stratified by goals_nominal)

```{r}
train_index <- createDataPartition(df_model$goals_nominal, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
train_data <- df_model[train_index, ]
test_data <- df_model[-train_index, ]
```
set.seed(42)

5. Set the Reference Level for the Nominal Factor
'Low_Goals' will serve as the baseline category for the log-odds comparisons

```{r}
train_data$goals_nominal <- relevel(train_data$goals_nominal, ref = "Low_Goals")
test_data$goals_nominal <- relevel(test_data$goals_nominal, ref = "Low_Goals")
```

6. Fit Multinomial Logistic Regression Model using nnet::multinom
Note: scaling numeric predictors beforehand can help convergence if scales differ vastly

```{r}
model <- multinom(goals_nominal ~ ., data = train_data, MaxNWts = 2000)
#View model summary (coefficients and standard errors)
summary(model)
```

7. Model Evaluation

```{r}
predictions <- predict(model, newdata = test_data)
# Generate confusion matrix and accuracy metrics
conf_matrix <- confusionMatrix(predictions, test_data$goals_nominal)
print(conf_matrix)
```

## AI Check 1
During AI given model correctly looks at the goals as ordinal values. By turning them into catagorical values. I would be cautious looking at the data, because of the way the values are just being dropped. By just dropping the data it might affect the model and the predictions there needs to be a different way to clean the data.



## AI Check 2
The goals are already somewhat ordinal, so maybe they just need to be ordered and catagorized. Then the predictors aren't scaled accurately all of the variables have different ranges and values and need to be standardized.
